description: A unique team that has unique and amazing curious members who love discovering space and new things.
summary:
Storyworld Museum is an interactive digital storytelling platform about the hardware NASA left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. Visitors begin at the Sun on an interactive solar system map (3D or 2D) and follow 13 historic hardware outward through a levels-and-progress map to track the completeness of each hardware journey. Astra, the cosmic guide character, walks visitors through an introductory video to the platform and every mission. Each hardware's story unfolds in five levels: name and basic information, history, scientific basis and mechanism, mission and reason behind it, and its status and legacy. Mission Control quizzes let visitors earn Space Historian badges.
It addresses the challenge by giving discarded equipment a voice. Instead of lists of facts, each piece of hardware gets a story through a space journey with verified NASA sources, archival photos, and NASA 3D models.
The reason this matters is that space knowledge and education quality is gradually decreasing due to the use of abstract and lifeless ways to express them. Therefore, it was crucial to create something that would change the way youth look at space and education. So instead of building an abstract way of learning, we built an engaging way of learning that is able to build strong and bright generations who are able to discover space. The museum makes the hardware legacy engaging and easy for students to understand.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
The museum guides visitors outward from the Sun across 13 checkpoints (4 on the Moon, 5 on Mars, 4 in deep space). Each machine has a five-act story with a timeline, 3D/2D mechanism lab, science explained in student-friendly analogies, final mission status and legacy. The site also includes an artifact archive with filters, an opening animated film, a 3D orbital map with a 2D fallback, and a Mission Control quiz with badges that needs no account.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT
It makes NASA mission history engaging for students and the general public by combining storytelling, character-driven narration and interactive visuals. Instead of dry facts, visitors feel the emotional side of machines that finished their work and stayed behind.



CREATIVITY
A single guide character, Astra, changes role and expression across the museum. The Solar System itself is the navigation, so exploring the site feels like a real expedition.


TOOLS
The website was built with Lovable. Images are hosted on Cloudinary. Slides were made in Canva. SI tools were used as described in the SI section.
tools used:
React 19 & TypeScript
TanStack Start & TanStack Router
Vite & Nitro
Tailwind CSS
Three.js
React Three Fiber (@react-three/fiber)
React Three Drei (@react-three/drei)
GSAP (GreenSock) & ScrollTrigger
Web Audio API (Procedural NASA Sound Synthesizer & SFX)
Web Speech API (Voiceover & Karaoke sync)
HTML5 Canvas 2D (Flying Starfield & 2D Mini-Games)
Lucide React (Icons)
Vitest & React Testing Library
Cloudinary (Media CDN)


FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
Accuracy (every story links to official NASA sources), accessibility (no account needed, 2D map if 3D fails, mobile-friendly layout), and honesty (the site clearly states it is an independent educational project and not an official NASA website).
